name: addERI_Proxmox_VE_Guest
description: Labels a Proxmox VE guest that is monitored as its own resource as a VirtualMachineResource, from its Proxmox MAC prefix. Needs no API token.
technicalNotes:
Always on. Applies to any Linux or Windows resource (isLinux() || isWindows()) whose auto.network.mac_address starts with Proxmox's default guest prefix bc:24:11 (either case: Windows reports it uppercase, SNMP lowercase), or that carries pve.guest.mac_prefix. Makes no API call and needs no token.

Why it exists: LogicMonitor's built-in addERI_Windows and addERI_Linux label a resource VirtualMachineResource only when one of its MACs carries an OUI on lm.data.topo's VM list, or its model or dmesg names a known hypervisor. bc:24:11 is on no list and a Proxmox guest reports a generic QEMU model, so every Proxmox guest monitored as its own resource -- Windows over WMI, Linux VM or LXC container over SNMP -- otherwise reads PhysicalServer.

Stamps one key, proxmoxve--vm--<lowercase MAC>, in its own category virt.proxmoxve at priority 3 with type VirtualMachineResource. Priority 3, because the resource type comes from the highest-priority ERI across categories, and the built-in net.l2 entry is priority 2 -- at priority 1 the key merges but the type stays PhysicalServer. The key joins nothing; the guest already meets its map vertex through the MAC net.l2 holds. topo.namespace and topo.blacklist are honoured through lm.topo, as in LogicMonitor's own addERI_* modules.

A cluster that hands out a different prefix (Datacenter > Options > MAC address prefix) sets pve.guest.mac_prefix on the group holding its guests, as a comma-separated list of prefixes (e.g. bc:24:11,02:00:00). The override replaces the default rather than adding to it, so list bc:24:11 too if it is still in use. A resource the property reaches whose MAC matches none of the prefixes is left untouched: the script prints nothing.

Not covered: guests whose NIC was given a hand-set MAC outside every configured prefix; guests whose resource reports a non-Proxmox MAC as its primary auto.network.mac_address (only that property is read); resources with no MAC at all, such as ping-only devices -- those are drawn on the map through Proxmox_VE_GuestStatus's instance ERIs, but get no resource label; and guests that are neither Linux nor Windows, such as virtual appliances (FortiGate-VM, pfSense/OPNsense, virtual routers), which are deliberately left to their own ERI modules rather than relabelled as plain VMs by MAC prefix alone.

Silent on no match and on any failure, like addCategory_Proxmox_VE: a PropertySource that prints on a resource it does not understand corrupts that resource's properties.

The isLinux() || isWindows() clause covers a Windows guest over WMI and a Linux VM or LXC container over SNMP. A new label can take up to 30 minutes (this module's interval) to land on the resource, and the topology map shows it after its next hourly run.
